name: GLM-OCR
purpose: Complex document understanding: parsing of text, formulas and tables, and information extraction to JSON; designed small for high-concurrency serving and edge deployment.

license.name: MIT (model, card section "License"); Apache-2.0 (GitHub repo LICENSE and PP-DocLayoutV3)
license.notes: HF repo has no LICENSE file; card says "The GLM-OCR model is released under the MIT License" and the pipeline uses PP-DocLayoutV3 (Apache-2.0). The zai-org/GLM-OCR GitHub LICENSE read is the unmodified Apache-2.0 text (code). Both permit commercial use and redistribution.

architecture.kind: encoder-decoder VLM with a layout-analysis stage (PP-DocLayout-V3) and parallel region recognition
architecture.why_this_design: Small decoder cuts latency and compute for high-concurrency and edge use; MTP loss and RL improve training efficiency; the two-stage layout-then-recognition pipeline handles complex tables, code-heavy pages and seals (card).

variants.notes: named in the llama.cpp PR; ggml-org is the llama.cpp organisation Files: Q8_0 0.95 GB, f16 1.79 GB, mmproj Q8_0 0.48 GB.

engine_support.notes: llama.cpp support merged 2026-02-18 (PR 19677); use the API with the specific prompts, the web UI degrades results

benchmarks.name: OmniDocBench v1.6 overall (third-party blog table)
benchmarks.harness: search summary of a third-party table, unverified

benchmarks.name: MDPBench overall (17 languages)
benchmarks.variant: GLM-OCR (Latin-script strong, non-Latin weak: Hindi 21.7, Thai 27.4)

strengths: information extraction to a JSON schema
German is listed on the card and third-party scores are good for its size (MDPBench DE 82.7)
weaknesses: prompts restricted to two supported scenarios
SDK only parses documents, not extraction
MDPBench: weak on non-Latin scripts (Hindi 21.7, Thai 27.4), irrelevant for German use
soft.maturity: Zhipu is an established vendor; model is a few months old

tona_fit.reason: MIT, 0.9B, German on the card and 82.7 on third-party German pages, official ggml-org GGUF; at least as good for German as the larger parsers. Missing Tona support is a blocker only.
blockers: Tona engine has no vision/OCR architecture; would run through llama.cpp

sources.note: MDPBench README table read directly; an earlier summarizer pass mislabeled the Latin-average column as DE, the DE values here come from the dataset README

pc-16gb.notes: BF16 about 2 GB; Tona runs one model at a time, so it replaces the resident model while it works
